sections.h2: Ways to sell a North Royalton house quickly
sections.html:
An owner can hire a broker, market the house without one, or sell to a cash buyer who absorbs the repairs. All three end at the same Cuyahoga County desk for transfer and recording, so the real choice is how much time and renovation you want to carry. Landlords have one more city step: a rental certificate for rented one, two and three family homes.

  • A broker listing suits a sound house when you can put up with tours and a buyer's inspection report.
  • Selling without an agent avoids commission but leaves the contract and deed work with you and your closing professional.
  • Cash suits estate houses, long-deferred repairs, empty rentals and tight moving dates.

North Royalton is a suburb in southern Cuyahoga County covering 21.32 square miles, with 31,322 residents at the 2020 census. The mid-2025 estimate is 30,936. The count has barely moved since 2010, when it was 30,444, so your house competes mainly with other established homes in a mature suburb. About seven in ten homes are lived in by their owners, and over nine in ten residents had not moved in the previous year.

sections.h2: Rental certificate and short-term rental limits
sections.html:
If the house is a rental, Chapter 1485 of the North Royalton codified ordinances requires a Certificate of Rental Registration from the Building Commissioner before anyone occupies it. The certificate is due by December 31 of the year before it applies, or within thirty days after the house first becomes a rental, and it cannot run past December 31 of the year it was issued. Multi-unit owners must renew every year or file an exemption form.

Timing sets the fee. A single-family rental registered by February 1 pays $50, and one filed after March 1 pays $125. An exemption form costs nothing before February 1 and $50 afterward. Skipping registration is a first-degree misdemeanor under the chapter.

Short-term rentals face tight limits. The chapter defines a short-term rental as any stay under thirty consecutive days. Tenant-occupied units cannot host transient guests at all. Owner-occupants may host for at most fourteen days a year, must live in the home at least 351 days a year, and need a transient rental registration certificate. A buyer who counted on nightly rental income needs to hear this before bidding.

State law adds a step when a rental changes hands. The county endorses the deed with a reminder that the new owner of residential rental property must file owner information with the auditor under Ohio Revised Code 5323.02.

sections.h2: How a sale is recorded in Cuyahoga County
sections.html:
Each transfer passes through the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Officer's Transfer and Recording division, which merged the former auditor, recorder and engineer roles. Real Estate Services insists that a transfer arrive with one of two forms: the DTE 100 value statement and receipt, or the DTE 100-EX, which states why the sale is exempt from the conveyance fee.

Since October 24, 2024 the standard recording fee has been $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each additional page, following Ohio Senate Bill 94. The division works from the fourth floor at 2079 E. Ninth Street in Cleveland, and weekday recording stops at 4 p.m. Staff cannot give legal advice, and the county notes that deed preparation counts as the practice of law, so a closing agent or lawyer should draft the deed.

Section 5302.30 of the Ohio code has sellers give buyers a property disclosure form promptly, with exemptions that include transfers by an estate fiduciary.

Inherited houses take special routes at the county. The conveyance standards describe an affidavit of real estate inherited under Ohio Revised Code 317.22, a probate court certificate of transfer, and a survivorship affidavit under 5302.17. A separate Great Estates Program page is aimed at families settling an estate.

Which paper you need depends on how title passed, so ask the probate court or your closing agent before you sign a contract with any buyer. Once the right document is in hand, the sale follows the same recording steps as any other.

sections.h2: Tax bills and the Board of Revision
sections.html:
County real estate bills run a year behind, so what is payable in one calendar year covers the year before. Bills come in two halves, and a 10 percent penalty attaches to an unpaid half. Call the County Treasurer for the current due dates rather than relying on last year's calendar.

At closing, the settlement agent splits the current bill between you and the buyer and pays any delinquency out of your proceeds. If the valuation looks too high, the county Board of Revision takes complaints each year until March 31, and sale papers such as a closing statement or the DTE 100 count as evidence. The board may raise a value when the evidence points that way, so file only if you have solid numbers.

sections.h2: Is a cash buyer worth a call?
sections.html:
For many owners the answer comes down to time and condition. A cash buyer takes the house as is, so you skip contractors, showings and a lender's appraisal. That helps with an estate that needs to close, a rental with a tenant problem or a move on a deadline.

Get any offer in writing and compare it with what a listing would leave you after commission and repairs. Ask who pays the recording fee, which date closes the sale, and whether the buyer will handle the rental certificate and county owner filing if the house was rented. A cash sale does not skip the deed, the DTE form or the title work.

faqs.q: Does a rented North Royalton house need a certificate?
faqs.a: Yes, if the house is a rental. Chapter 1485 bars anyone from occupying a residential rental unit unless a current Certificate of Rental Registration has been issued, and the certificate expires each December 31. Keep it current while tenants live there.

faqs.q: Where is a North Royalton deed filed?
faqs.a: At the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Officer's Transfer and Recording division, with a DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX attached. Recording costs $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page beyond that.

faqs.q: Are nightly rentals allowed in North Royalton?
faqs.a: Only in narrow cases. Owners living in the home 351 or more days a year may host guests up to fourteen days annually with a registration certificate. Tenant-occupied units may not host them.

faqs.q: What is the penalty on a late Cuyahoga County tax bill?
faqs.a: Ten percent is added to an unpaid half-year bill. Ask the Treasurer for the due dates that apply this year.

faqs.q: What if I inherited the North Royalton house?
faqs.a: Title reaches the heirs through a probate court certificate or an affidavit of real estate inherited, and the county lists both routes in its conveyance standards. An heir who did not live in the house within the past year is generally excused from the Ohio disclosure form, but should confirm with a closing agent.
